metadata.description: A running service of containers and/or systemd units, with replicas and endpoints, realized and managed by a provider. A Base by the Base test: the Open Application Model workload, TOSCA's node and Kubernetes workload resources abstract a running set of constituents (CLS-002). A Kubernetes provider, a podman host or a systemd host fills an order here. Named for what a provider yields, not the act (a Service is the act). Secrets are never inline; env and mounts reference a CredentialRef.

service_kind.description: Coarse classification for grouping and ordering: `application`, `infrastructure_daemon` (shuts down after applications), `database`, `gateway`, `registry`, `monitoring`, `fleet_manager` (the multi-cluster management plane; shuts down after the clusters it manages), `other`.

constituents.description: The workloads that make up the service: a Container by reference, or a host plus its systemd units.

container_ref.description: Reference to Container — the container realizing this constituent. Common-elements Reference shape (handle string or {uuid, handle} object); resolvable and policy-walkable, never an opaque string.

host.description: handle of the host/VM the systemd units run on (form=systemd).

replicas.description: Desired instance count; 0 means intentionally scaled down.

exposure.description: The ask to be reached over the network: the `names` consumers should reach it at and the `visibility` it is meant to have. Stated, never inferred: a workload with no `exposure` asked for none, and a gate compares this ask with the `endpoints` the provider reports (row 166).

names.description: Hostnames consumers reach the service at (dav.example.com). The provider publishes where each resolves in `endpoints`; the zone record is DNSZone's.

visibility.description: How far the service is meant to be reachable: `loopback` (its own host), `internal` (the estate's networks), `external` (the internet). The same codelist Container `network.ports` uses. A security fact, so it is declared here and never derived from where the service happens to run.

protocols.description: Application protocols the service is meant to serve (https, imaps, ssh). Open codelist.

endpoints.description: How the service is reached, as the provider reports it once Realized. An output, not an element: a consumer asks for exposure, the provider says where (row 116). Each entry names the mechanism (`via`) and the address; `visibility` is set only by a collector that can see the boundary (the gateway), never guessed from the address (row 166).

name.description: The endpoint's name within the service (web, api, imaps).

url.description: Full URL when the protocol has one (https://dav.example.com/).

host.description: Hostname or address when there is no URL form.

protocol.description: Application or transport protocol (https, imaps, tcp). Open codelist.

via.description: The mechanism that exposes it: a Kubernetes `route` or `ingress`, a `load_balancer` service, a `node_port`, a container's `published_port`, a process `listener` on a host, or a gateway `port_forward`.

visibility.description: Reach as observed at the boundary, the same codelist as `exposure.visibility`. Absent when the collector could not see it.

relationships.name: runs_on
relationships.description: Runs on a cluster (its container constituents are scheduled there). TOSCA HostedOn.

relationships.name: runs_on
relationships.description: Or runs directly on a host (native systemd units / rootless containers).

relationships.name: uses_storage
relationships.description: External storage the service uses (also StorageCluster / FileShare). TOSCA DependsOn.

relationships.name: requires
relationships.description: Service-to-service dependency (strength hard|soft) — e.g. an app requiring an auth service.

relationships.name: requires
relationships.description: Requires a directory/identity service — strength hard|soft.

relationships.name: requires
relationships.description: Requires a DNS/DHCP address service — strength hard|soft.
Binds to a database's connection outputs. TOSCA BindsTo.
Secrets consumed by the service's constituents — no secret material inline (DCM ADR-023).

adopts.role: service-as-composed-nodes shape, the typed relationship vocabulary for runs_on / requires / binds_to, and the Endpoint capability (protocol, port, secure, network_name) that grounds `exposure` and `endpoints`
grounds `constituents[]` — an application is a set of component workloads, one level up from Container
realization vocabulary for Kubernetes-hosted services — naturalized by the provider, not restated

context.purpose: Models a logical running service — one or more containers and/or systemd units acting as one thing — so application-level dependencies carry order.
context.plain_description: The application layer: the mail service, the registry, model serving — a named service, classified by its required `service_kind` (application, infrastructure_daemon, database, and kin), composed of `constituents` that each declare their `form`: a `container` constituent references its container record via `container_ref`; a `systemd` constituent names its `host` and `units`. It declares what the service needs — a database, a directory, name service, storage, another service, each dependency hard or soft — which is what makes infrastructure-daemons-stop-after-applications derivable. `exposure` states the names and visibility it asks for; the `endpoints` output says where the provider put it; readiness is a status condition.
use_when: You need an application composed of several workloads treated as one node with one dependency surface.
You need service-to-service and service-to-infrastructure dependencies (with hard/soft strength) to drive shutdown/startup order.
You need host services (systemd units) and containerized services modeled uniformly.
not_for: A single container's runtime spec — Container; the service references containers as constituents.
The database a service uses — Database, referenced as a dependency.
works_with: KubernetesCluster / Machine.BareMetalHost / Machine.VM — where the constituents run.
Database / DirectoryService / AddressService — what the service requires.
CredentialRef — the service's secrets, by reference.
